# Population pyramid

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Mirrored ordered bands on one shared scale: band geometry is validated for equal width and contiguity, and the youngest band is rendered at the bottom no matter which way the data was authored. Type `pyramid`. Aliases: `age-pyramid`, `population-pyramid`.

## Use cases

- Population by age and sex
- Mirrored distribution
- Customer age by gender

## Chart IDs

One form; its chart ID is `pyramid`.

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "pyramid",
  "data": {
    "bands": [
      { "id": "junior", "from": 0, "to": 5 },
      { "id": "senior", "from": 5, "to": 10 },
      { "id": "long", "from": 10, "to": 15 }
    ],
    "groups": [
      { "id": "north", "label": "North", "values": [40, 30, 20] },
      { "id": "south", "label": "South", "values": [35, 25, 15] }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
    "title": "North has more employees in every tenure band",
    "unit": "employees",
    "source": "Illustrative data"
  }
}
```

## Data

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| bands | array | yes | Contiguous ordered bands, each with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds; only the last may be open-ended. |
| bands[].id | string | yes | Unique ordered-band identity used by keyed group values. |
| bands[].from | number | yes | Inclusive lower bound. |
| bands[].to | number |  | EXCLUSIVE upper bound; contiguity is bands[i].to === bands[i+1].from. Omit on the LAST band only, to declare it open-ended. |
| bands[].label | string |  | Authored band caption; omission derives a caption from its bounds. |
| groups | array | yes | Exactly two groups displayed on opposite sides using the same scale. |
| groups[].id | string | yes | Group identity for one side of the population pyramid. |
| groups[].label | string |  | Displayed group name; defaults to its id. |
| groups[].date | string |  | ISO observation date for dated group comparisons. CAGR needs a positive date interval; age-band bounds do not supply time. |
| groups[].values | array | yes | Counts or amounts, one per band. Shares are DERIVED: a percent cell, a null, a negative or a non-finite value is refused with its own error code. |
| groups[].values[].bandId | string | yes | Band id identifying this group value independently of array position. |
| groups[].values[].value | number \| null | yes | Raw count or amount for the band; percentages are derived. Null is refused during layout. |
| groups[].colorRole | string |  | Theme color role for this group of pyramid bars. One of good, bad, warn, neutral, neutralLight, highlight, total, others; series-N for step N of the theme ramp, 1-based (series-2 is color.series[1]); or status-<key> for a theme status colour. A hex colour goes in fill. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| basis | string | `'count'`, `'shareOfTotal'` | `'count'` | Default 'count'. 'shareOfTotal' divides by the grand total across BOTH groups and all bands — never per group, which would hide the group-size imbalance a pyramid is read for. |
| methodNote | boolean |  |  | Default false. true adds the method footnote stating the band convention: [from, to), youngest at the bottom, equal widths. An open-ended top band and the share base are required for interpretation and print regardless. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `detailFields`, `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `rowLabels`, `sort`, `topN`, `hatchStrength`, `colorblindSafe`, `rounding`.

## Annotations

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.

| Kind | Purpose | Required | Anchors | Optional fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cagr | Draws a growth arrow between two anchored points and computes the compound annual growth rate from their values and ISO-date span. |  | from: AnchorRef (optional); to: AnchorRef (optional) | suffix: string, default 'p.a.'. Text after the rate. period: boolean. Print the period before the rate from the anchors' category labels, '2014–2019: +5.8% p.a.'. Default true when the chart carries two or more CAGRs, so nested brackets are told apart by their text, false otherwise. An arrow's ends show its span, so an arrow prints the rate alone unless period is true. shape: bracket \| arrow, default bracket. arrow draws one straight arrow over the marks with the rate in an oval on it, lifted until it clears them. Where no straight line clears the chart, the span is too short for the oval, a stack's inner layer is the anchor or the chart lays comparisons out itself, it draws the bracket and warns cagr-arrow-no-room. | Omitted endpoints span the first to the last category, or the first to the last total on a waterfall. Resolved endpoints need a positive date interval from ISO dates or year-bearing labels and a positive start value; an end of zero reads -100%, and a start at or below zero or a negative end omits the rate and warns cagr-undefined. On a continuous time axis the years are the exact span between the two readings. An anchor on one series of several (seriesId, or a line category, which reads the first drawn series) names that series in the label, "Product B +10.1% p.a.", and the arm runs from that series' segment or point. In text, ${value} prints the rate with its suffix, so "CAGR 2014–2019: ${value}" keeps the computed number. |
| diff | Draws a level-difference arrow between two anchors and computes either percent change or their signed value difference. | from, to | from: AnchorRef; to: AnchorRef | mode: relative \| absolute \| reversed, default relative. relative prints the percent change from 'from' to 'to', reversed the change from 'to' to 'from', absolute the value difference. | Mode defaults to relative. Relative and reversed changes need a nonzero base; negative bases use its absolute magnitude and emit a warning. Absolute mode reports the raw value difference. A hidden label removes its arm. |
| delta | Computes the signed difference between an anchored value and another anchor or literal, then places a collision-managed label at the first anchor. | at, vs | at: AnchorRef; vs: AnchorRef \| number |  |  |
| note | Places authored text at an anchored data element through collision avoidance, with an optional icon or status chip. | at, text | at: AnchorRef |  |  |
| callout | Places authored free text at an anchored data element, routing a leader when displaced and honoring the preferred side. | at, text | at: AnchorRef | preferSide: left \| right \| above \| below. Side the solver tries first; the label keeps a leader when it moves. headline: string. A bold first line over the text, which then prints in plain type; ${value} in it prints the anchored value from the data. Example: "headline": "${value}", "text": "Peak in handheld-loom demand" prints 153 in bold over the words. arrow: boolean, default false. A thin arrow from the text to the anchored point; the first line sits level with the point, right or left of it, where there is room. Not with icon or status. Example: "arrow": true. |  |

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 270 px; fit `fill`.
Below 270 px high, down to the compact floor of 280 × 180 px, the chart draws in compact mode; `belowMinimum: 'refuse'` refuses there instead.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).

| workforce-tenure-gender | example | Women outnumber men below four years of tenure and are outnumbered above ten |

| dated-population-comparison | example | Growth within the same age band across two observation dates |
| dated-share-difference | example | An absolute difference between shares is measured in percentage points |

## Not for

More than two groups or unordered bands; pyramid mirrors two groups over contiguous ordered bands.
